expectations.note: Playing 07-undercover-44 (parent /opt/nothingness/media) while browsing the different parent folder /opt/nothingness, the jump glyph was present; tapping void-crumb-jump-to-playing navigated the browser into /opt/nothingness/media and left track 44's row on screen (idx10, y4-45 within viewport 0-332).

With /opt/nothingness/media already open but track 44's row scrolled off the top (reverse ListView, scrollPosition 0), the glyph was present; tapping it scrolled the list to scrollPosition 127 bringing row 44 fully into view (y4-45) while currentPath stayed /opt/nothingness/media (no re-navigation).

The action is not conditioned on visibility: on Linux the code sets showJumpGlyph = playingExists unconditionally. With track 44's row fully visible and unclipped (y4-45 inside viewport 0-332) the jump action was still exposed as an active tappable button (SemanticsNode#9, actions tap/longPress, label 'jump to now-playing track in browser'). This is the always-on pattern the expectation falsifies.

With nothing playing (isPlaying false, songInfo null) no jump action appeared in tree or semantics at /opt/nothingness/media, and re-checked at the /opt/nothingness parent folder with the same result.

getSemantics returned a real tree (not the generic-unavailable response); the action node carries the distinguishing label 'jump to now-playing track in browser' plus the ⊙ glyph, with tap action — a genuine accessible affordance, not a bare glyph.

Candidate's before_track_54.png plainly shows the browser with the playing row (title 54) absent from the visible list (rows 44-52 shown) and the ⊙ glyph in the crumb; my live before-state reproduction (playing 44 off-screen, rows 47-54 shown) confirms the same pre-activation condition.

Candidate's after_track_54_delayed.png shows row 54 now visible and highlighted with path /opt/nothingness/media unchanged; my live after-state reproduction shows the same — row 44 scrolled into view at top, folder path identical.

The write-up's claims (glyph only when playing; shown on Linux even in the same folder; tap keeps folder and scrolls via scrollToTrack; before/after screenshots) are all backed by session observations: 6 getLibraryState, 6 getSemantics, 18 tree, 68 shoot, plus the before/after PNGs it captured.

On-screen taps navigate correctly: tapping void-folder:/opt/nothingness/media entered media, tapping void-up returned to /opt/nothingness. Playback transitions behave normally: with a real folder queue (row tap builds 10-track queue), next advanced 46->47 and prev returned 47->46; pause/resume toggled cleanly. (next/prev stopping under a single-track play is the pre-existing empty-queue quirk, not a regression.)

Overflow count stayed 0 across E1-E4 exercises; the only run-log errors are environmental ALSA sound-card warnings (no audio device in container), no Flutter exceptions. App remained live and responsive (library registered, inspect answering) at the end.
